chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from whoever mentioned it, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
'Then let the human being look at his food.'
I said: 'What is his food?' He said: 'His knowledge which he is taking — from whom he is taking it.'

key_terms.طَعَام: Food; here interpreted metaphorically as knowledge/spiritual nourishment
key_terms.عِلْم: Knowledge, particularly religious and spiritual knowledge
key_terms.يَأْخُذُ: To take/receive; indicating the act of acquiring knowledge from a teacher

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about the source of knowledge in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) interprets the Quranic verse 80:24 — 'Then let the human being look at his food' — not literally, but as a metaphor for intellectual and spiritual sustenance. The Imam explains that a person's 'food' is the knowledge they receive, and the critical concern is: from whom is that knowledge being taken? This teaching emphasizes the necessity of scrutinizing the sources of religious knowledge, a central concern in Shia epistemology where the legitimacy of the transmitter is as vital as the content transmitted.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Zayd Al Shahaam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [80:24]
Then let the human being look at his food.
I said, ‘What is his food?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His knowledge which he is taking, from who he is taking it’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from one he mentioned from Zayd al-Shahham from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following.
“It is his knowledge that he acquires from whoever he acquires.”
This he said in answer to the question ‘What is his food’ in the words of Allah, “Let the human being think about (how We produce) his food.” [80:24]?’
